# Public-Claim Limitation Matrix

**Internal, generated, not deployed.** An internal claim-control system. It does not validate the research, the Engine, privacy controls, commercial readiness or production use. Generated by `tools/claim-provenance/build.mjs` from `lib/categories.js`. Do not edit by hand.

**Two different permissions.** "May state a factual historic result" means a dated result may be reported with its sample, window and limitation. "May market a current capability" would mean presenting it as something JRS or the Engine does now. No research category below permits the second.

| Claim category | What may be said | What must accompany it | What must not be said | Historic result or current capability |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| JRS methodology | What the five review conditions ask, and that the methodology is under study. Descriptive results with their study, date and sample. | The five conditions are not psychometrically validated. Associations between the conditions and the overall determination are expected by construction. | That JRS is a validated, independently validated or psychometrically validated standard; that the conditions discriminate, on the strength of p-values from the condition and determination association. | May describe the method. May not market validation. |
| Constructed detection findings | A factual historic result: 16 reviewers, 24 constructed records, 384 graded reads, mean accuracy 83.9 percent (95 percent CI 72.7 to 95.1, participant level), data lock 15 August 2026; sensitivity 87.0 percent and specificity 80.7 percent; reviewer range 37.5 to 100 percent. | Constructed corpus and author-generated reference classification; mean of reviewer scores; not reliability and not field performance; the reviewer-level spread. | Accuracy on real records; a reliability or agreement figure; any per-reviewer expectation from the mean; any Engine performance figure. | May state a factual historic result. May not market a current detection capability. |
| Reviewer agreement findings | A factual historic result from a separate 10-record sample: Gwet's AC1 0.739 (invited experts) and 0.623 (regular reviewers), with the pre-registered criterion not met. | Separate and smaller sample; 10 records; analytic lower bounds 0.402 and 0.252 against the required 0.41; interim. | That reviewers reliably agree; a verbal band such as "substantial"; agreement as correctness or as psychometric validation. | May state a factual historic result. May not market reliability. |
| Cross-model agreement findings | Factual historic consistency figures, each with its own denominator and window: 61 runs (12 June to 21 August 2026, 66.7 to 93.3 percent, mean 85.3 percent); 37 runs at the full 15-record set as read on 13 August 2026 (82.2 to 93.3 percent); 41 runs at the 15 August 2026 data lock. | Raw agreement only; the reproducibility criterion is not established because the required AC1 was not computed; the denominator and window of the figure used. | Accuracy, human reliability or independent validation; swapping one run count for another; a single "latest" run as the result. | May state a factual historic result. May not market model accuracy or reproducibility. |
| Participant geography and participation counts | 58 international reviewers across three studies; 36 completed the full 24-record set across 16 countries; the detection panel was 16 reviewers in 11 countries. | Which group each count describes. Participation is acknowledgment, not a result. | That participants validated, endorsed or confirmed JRS; mixing the 16-country and 11-country figures. | May state participation. May not present it as endorsement. |
| Local Engine development | That a controlled local-development candidate exists; that its repository tests use a mock adapter and constructed records; that public review routes refuse submissions. | Mock adapter; constructed development records; not a measure of accuracy, reliability or validity; no provider called. | That the Engine is tested on real records, evaluated, accurate, validated or ready; any research figure as Engine evidence. | May describe development status. May not market a capability. |
| Source-grounding controls | That local tests check each candidate quotation occurs exactly in the record, and that unlocatable quotations are withheld. | Exact quotation presence is not semantic support; an anchor shows where text sits, not that it supports the finding. | That findings are correct, verified, hallucination-free or semantically supported because they are quoted. | Internal only. |
| Public resources and training | What the materials teach and how to begin, with guidance quantities presented as guidance. | Guidance quantities (records to start with, group sizes) are not research findings. | Guidance numbers phrased as measured results; certification or qualification claims. | May describe the materials. May not present guidance as evidence. |
| Privacy and security history | Historical data flows as history; the current position that no route accepts record text. | Historical labelling; whether stored output remains is NOT ESTABLISHED; a written policy does not prove a live control. | Historical data flows in the present tense; that data is "secure" or that a control operates, without operator evidence. | May state history and current route status. May not market security. |
| Controlled evaluation discussions | That no release gate has passed and no evaluation access is offered. | Every gate is BLOCKED or NOT_ASSESSED; any future evaluation needs a new owner instruction. | That an evaluation is available, under way or passed; that research results stand in for an Engine evaluation. | May state the gate status. May not offer an evaluation. |
| Future commercial or acquisition language | That no licensing, sale or acquisition pathway is offered. | Rights and title are not established; any future pathway requires owner authorization and legal review. | Licensing-ready, sale-ready, acquisition-ready, or any offer to license, sell or acquire. | Never. |
| DRR studies about AI drafting | Study results with their reader, sample and scope. | Who or what the reader was, the number of texts, and that it is research about AI drafting tools, not Engine output or a DRR score. | A human-reader result where the reader was a model; an Engine or DRR-score figure. | May state a factual historic result. May not market a measurement capability. |
| Publication and editorial status | An acceptance only where the venue's decision is on file, named with its venue type. | Venue type (practitioner magazine or journal); whether the acceptance is documented by the venue or only by the author's file. | A target venue as an acceptance; an invitation to revise as an acceptance; a magazine acceptance as peer review. | May state documented publication. May not imply peer-reviewed validation. |

Claim cards for each category: `docs/architecture/claim-cards/`. Claims behind each category: `CLAIM_EVIDENCE_REGISTER.md`.
